business_scope.primary_industry_name: Programmatic Real-Time Ad Exchange and SSP Platform

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Quebec is a mixed jurisdiction — private law, including partnership law and property, is governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (civilian tradition), while federal public, tax, securities, and commercial regulation follow common law doctrines; procedural law is codified but interpreted co-relative with common law principles.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement (CUSMA), in force July 1, 2020 (investment chapter: national treatment, MFN, investor protections)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union, provisionally applied since 2017
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada since December 30, 2018
Convention between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1980), as amended by the Fourth and Fifth Protocols and the OECD Multilateral Instrument
Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, in force April 1, 2021

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The controlling instruments are: (i) An Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises (ARE), CQLR c E-6.1, ss. 27-34 (declaration of registration, establishment, and register of ultimate beneficiaries) and its implementing Regulation respecting the declaration of information on ultimate beneficiaries, CQLR c E-6.1, r 1.1; (ii) Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236-2261 (société en commandite / limited partnership); (iii) Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; (iv) FINTRAC interpretive guidance on CDD and beneficial ownership; (v) Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, and Regulation respecting the requirements for names of enterprises, CQLR c E-6.1, r 2; (vi) Canada's sanctions architecture: Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2, and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 10, together with orders and regulations administered by Global Affairs Canada.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney of each non-resident general partner (procuration) authorising the Quebec-based attorney or agent to execute the declaration of registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or commissioner for oaths in the partner's country of residence, or a Quebec notary where the partner appears by counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Convention of 5 October 1961 issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; consular legalization required only if the origin state is not a Hague Party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner (any individual holding 25% or more) and of each general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating passport authority or notarizing official of the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign-issued documents; for Canadian-issued identity documents, a certified true copy by a Quebec notary is sufficient, optionally apostilled by the Ministère des Relations internationales et de la Francophonie (Quebec apostille service)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or current extract from the company register of any corporate general partner or corporate UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the foreign state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, followed by certified French translation by a member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec (OTTIAQ)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/UBO due diligence file: PEP, OFAC, UN Security Council, and Global Affairs Canada sanctions screening reports on all partners and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Compliance screening provider registered in Canada or supervising legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not subject to apostille; must be dated and signed by the screening officer, kept in the REQ-compliant partnership records, and certified by counsel when shared with financial institutions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screening is mandatory and must cover, at minimum: (i) all foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates under ss. 11.12-11.14 of the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; (ii) domestic PEPs and Heads of International Organizations for any high-value wire or ACH transactions; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, and Global Affairs Canada's consolidated Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iv) any counterparty of the programmatic AdTech exchange where a geographic-risk or sanctions exposure is non-trivial; and (v) all false-positive hits must be independently confirmed and documented before onboarding, with re-confirmation at intervals not exceeding 12 months.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online services via www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca, including the name-analysis module ("Aide à la recherche et à la rédaction d'un nom d'entreprise") and the central enterprise register (Registre des entreprises).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Regulation respecting the requirements for names of enterprises (CQLR c E-6.1, r 2), a limited partnership registered in Quebec must adopt a name in French. The name may be accompanied by an English version, a version in a third language, or a transliteration in another script only where the French version is equally prominent or one of the statutory exceptions applies (recognised autonomous trademark, linguistic exemptions granted by the Office québécois de la langue française). The legal designation must clearly indicate a limited partnership: "société en commandite" or "S.E.C." in French, with "L.P." or "Limited Partnership" permitted in the English version. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must not cause confusion with existing names in the REQ register or in the Canadian trademark register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Trust, Fiducie (prior authorization of the Autorité des marchés financiers and the Superintendent of Financial Institutions)
Assurance, Insurance, Réassurance (prior AMF licence or Minister of Finance approval)
Université, Collège, École (authorization of the Ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur or the Ministère de l'Éducation)
Hôpital, Hospital, Clinique (authorization of the Ministère de la Santé et des Services sociaux)
Avocat, Notaire, Architecte, Ingénieur, Médecin, Comptable professionnel agréé (reserved titles protected by the Professional Code and the relevant professional orders)
Croix-Rouge, Red Cross, Organisation des Nations Unies, United Nations, Interpol (misleading or statutorily reserved public emblems)
Canada, Québec, Gouvernement du Canada, Gouvernement du Québec (only with explicit authorization or where the enterprise is genuinely governmental)
Bourse, Commission des valeurs mobilières, Securities Commission (unlawfully suggests a regulator or securities exchange licence)
Société anonyme, Inc., Ltd., Corp., LLC (indicators of a different legal form inconsistent with a Limited Partnership)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire refuses the declared name, the Registrar issues a written notice citing the statutory ground under ARE ss. 37-38 and the name regulation. The filer may: (1) modify the proposed name and re-file within 10 business days using the same declaration and payment receipt; or (2) contest by filing a written 'demande de révision' with the REQ within 30 days of the notice, attaching the REQ notice and a legal memorandum demonstrating distinctiveness and compliance with the French-language and transliteration requirements of the regulation; or (3) if the review is unfavourable, apply to the Court of Québec by way of an action to annul the Registraire's decision within the ordinary three-year prescriptive period read with art. 529 of the Code of Civil Procedure; the court may order registration where the refusal is unreasonable. Where the rejection concerns a sensitive token, the SOP first requires securing the competent ministerial authorization in the form of an attestation letter and annexing it to the re-filed declaration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible for this AdTech/SSP segment. The ARE requires every enterprise carrying on activities in Quebec to hold an establishment in Quebec and to declare its address; a serviced office or virtual-office address staffed during business hours may satisfy the registration if mail is accepted, records are physically accessible to the partners, and the address allows service of process. Pure mailbox-forwarding addresses without any human contact are not accepted by REQ and will be rejected or struck. For banking and AML purposes, correspondent banks and the target SWIFT/ACH rails may require documentary evidence of operating substance; a virtual office without local management generally triggers enhanced KYC but remains permissible where a Quebec general partner or counsel office is maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-zero. For a non-licensed, low-risk AdTech exchange domiciled in a serviced or virtual office, the quantified annual probability of an unannounced REQ on-site inspection is estimated at under 5%. The risk rises to approximately 15-18% in the first tax year where Revenu Québec conducts registration audits of partnerships with 100% non-resident UBOs, and to approximately 25% where a FINTRAC suspicious-transaction report or a foreign tax-administration request implicates the partnership; in such cases, inspection may be coordinated with the RCMP and municipal licensing authorities under the Canadian AML/CFT framework.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Regulation respecting the fees of the Registraire des entreprises, CQLR c E-6.1, r 9

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Declaration of registration of the limited partnership (immatriculation d'une société en commandite) filed within 10 days of constitution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (currently CAD 89-99) based on the filing delay; converted at 1.35 CAD/USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec notary fees for certification of partnership declaration, partners' resolutions, and notarized powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary in private practice (Ordre des notaires du Québec tariff)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing tariff-based notarial fees in Quebec (CAD 250-350 average for a standard certification and intervention)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille of foreign UBO and/or corporate general partner documents (per document, where partners are non-Canadian)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authority (e.g., US Department of State or state secretary; UK FCDO; etc.) or Global Affairs Canada for Canadian documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International and consular fee schedules; varies USD 15-60 per apostille; USD 35 used as blended benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of all foreign UBO and corporate filings by OTTIAQ-certified translator (average 6-8 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CAD 12-18 per page plus minimum order charge; USD 120 represents the projected bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing report and consolidated PEP/OFAC/UN/Global Affairs Canada sanctions screening for all partners and 25%+ ultimate beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: FINTRAC-compliant screening provider or qualifying counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional benchmark for low-risk corporate UBO screening under FINTRAC CDD guidance (USD 250-450)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite), partner registers, UBO statements, and Stage-1 pre-incorporation legal opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat-fee market benchmark for a cross-border single-tier LP with two or fewer UBOs and standard ISIC 7310 AdTech scope (USD 1,500-2,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization contingency for any UBO document originating in a non-Hague (non-Convention) jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Embassy or consulate legalization section of the document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedules plus diplomatic courier handling; shown as a full USD 600 earnest-cost reserve to protect the filing timeline

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Integrated Quebec and federal registration event (NEQ/BN issuance and provincial tax account setup where the LP elects an instant-filing scenario)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (joint business registry integration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Zero statutory fee; the integrated federal-provincial registration is free of charge

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, Articles 2202–2237 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, sections 4 and 22; Regulation respecting fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Service de l'immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite / Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Québec limited partnership; contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement and may be made in cash or property. No escrow account is imposed by the general statute, but the general partner must segregate capital records and maintain partnership bank accounts in the name of the partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner approves the initial limited partnership agreement and accepts the capital subscriptions of the initial limited partners as recorded in the partnership register. RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be established at 1000 Rue de la Montagne, Montréal, QC, and the undersigned officer is appointed as manager with authority to open bank accounts, sign electronic transactions, and instruct counsel. RESOLVED, that the manager shall file the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, remit the statutory fee, and complete all ancillary filings. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers and counsel are authorized to implement this resolution and carry on business in accordance with the Civil Code of Québec and applicable advertising regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preliminary Name Reservation and Legal Sufficiency Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Online Name Verification Module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed limited partnership name through the Registraire's online platform, including the mandatory legal ending 'L.P.' or 'société en commandite'. If the name is distinctive and compliant, receive an advice or reservation confirmation; otherwise, amend the name and resubmit. The general partner must also confirm that the proposed name does not infringe upon protected trade-marks.
required_dossiers: Proposed Name and Legal Designation
Descriptive Business Activities in ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810
Contact Information of the General Partner
Name Search Report or Online Verification Result
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised declaration of proposed name; if the refusal persists, seek a review by the Registraire under the Act respecting legal publicity or make an application to the court of competent jurisdiction for judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Capital Contribution Schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal Counsel / Notary for any non-monetary contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement, identifying the general partner and limited partners, profit-sharing ratios, management powers, and capital contribution schedule. For contributions in kind, obtain a notarial statement and ensure a compliant valuation. Record all contributions in the partnership ledger and in the initial capital subscription register.
required_dossiers: Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Executed Subscription Schedules
Identification and Address Details of All Partners
Valuation Certificate for Non-Cash Contributions (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise and re-execute the agreement to cure disclosure deficiencies; for contested valuations, commission an independent appraiser and re-file the valuation certificate with the partnership records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Registration with the Québec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Online Filing Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the application for registration of a limited partnership through the Registraire's secure portal. Provide the registered office address, the general partner's legal identification, list of limited partners, description of business activities, and information on any representative elected to the Registraire. Pay the statutory fee online and retain the electronic acknowledgment.
required_dossiers: Completed Déclaration d'immatriculation
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Proof of General Partner's Existence or Authorization
Registered Office Address Acceptance
Payment Receipt / Transaction Reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a request for information or correction, submit an amended declaration and pay any correction fee; if the application is refused, remedy the stated grounds and file a fresh declaration before taking further judicial appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registrations (CRA and Revenu Québec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the partnership's business number with the CRA and obtain the Québec enterprise number (NEQ) as issued by the Registraire. As needed, register for GST/HST and QST accounts, and for payroll accounts if the partnership intends to hire employees. File the registration through the relevant online business registration service or transmit a signed authorization to a representative.
required_dossiers: Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
Execution Copy of the Limited Partnership Agreement
Identification Documents of the General Partner
Bank Account Information for the Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or rejected, contact the CRA Business Registration Service or Revenu Québec to reconcile name and jurisdiction details; if the denial is due to missing source documents, resubmit the complete dossier and, where necessary, request a formal reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Activation, Corporate Records, and Compliance Intake
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the registered office at the declared address, retain the partnership minute book, and prepare the initial resolutions, officer log, and AML/KYC assessment. Confirm the data processing and privacy compliance framework consistent with federal PIPEDA and Québec's Law 25, and record the identity of the compliance officer responsible for advertising platform operations.
required_dossiers: Registered Office Lease or Owner Authorization
Partnership Minute Book / Register of Partners
Initial Compliance Manual and Risk Assessment
Privacy Officer Appointment Form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is rejected or later changed, file an application for amendment with the Registraire des entreprises and update the partnership records; any unresolved compliance deficiency must be raised with counsel and corrected before the partnership commences active operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810 — a programmatic real-time ad exchange and SSP platform is a non-physical service activity. If a physical office is later established, the local city or borough permit authority (e.g., City of Montréal Permit and Inspection Service) may require an ordinary occupancy permit; no Québec industrial licensing board supervision applies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating or manufacturing license is mandatory for a programmatic ad exchange platform. A standard municipal commercial occupancy permit may be required for office premises, but this is outside the ad exchange industrial scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration not required — the service activity does not fall within the listed categories of the Québec Environmental Impact Assessment Regulation; no contaminant discharge or land disturbance is associated with an AdTech SSP platform.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the information-service business. To the extent the partnership later leases equipped premises, wastewater and ventilation discharges must remain within municipal sewer and Quebec clean-air bylaws; commercial tenants must also comply with the City of Montréal noise, waste sorting, and e-waste recycling standards. No VOC or industrial effluent thresholds apply to software-based ad exchange operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required at formation without physical premises. If a commercial office is occupied, the partnership must obtain a fire safety attestation and emergency evacuation plan from the municipal fire prevention service, undergo any required structural load verification for commercial tenants, and file evidence of workplace health and safety compliance with the CNESST, including medical and hazardous-product clearance, as applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST, income tax, and payroll; online portal: Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business.html) and CRA My Business Account. Revenu Québec (RQ) for Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec income tax, and Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ); online portal: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/ (Mon dossier d'entreprise).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Quebec Limited Partnership (société en commandite) is established by filing a declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the 10-digit NEQ. Thereafter: (1) obtain the 9-digit federal CRA Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online using Form RC1WB/RCI; (2) activate the GST/HST 'RT' account (mandatory once annual worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 or immediately for non-resident suppliers of digital services above the quarterly threshold); (3) activate the payroll 'RP/RC' account if employees are hired; (4) register the LP with Revenu Québec for the QST account (TVQ) and, if applicable, QPIP/QPP payroll accounts; (5) because the LP is fiscally transparent, the partnership itself files T5013/CO-17 information returns while each partner reports its allocable share of income on its own return; non-resident partners must obtain no separate entity-level TIN but must file a Canadian income tax return and may need a BN if carrying on business in Canada. All registrations can be completed online in one session via the CRA BRO 'One-stop' link to Revenu Québec for Quebec-based businesses.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — Canadian limited partnerships are fiscally transparent for federal and Quebec income tax purposes (ITA s. 96; Taxation Act, Quebec). The LP computes income notionally as a separate person solely for allocation to general and limited partners; the LP is not a taxable entity. For QST purposes the partnership is treated as a single registrant/person (A.R.Q.S.T. s. 38.1) and must register separately for the QST account. The Active Business Income earned through the LP retains its character for partners, and non-resident partners are taxable in Canada under Part I on their share of Canadian-source partnership income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Canada; fiscal transparency is statutory and cannot be waived. Relevant partnership elections: (i) joint election under ITA s. 97(2) for a partner to transfer property to the LP on a tax-deferred rollover at adjusted cost base; (ii) election under ITA s. 96 for a non-calendar fiscal period for the partnership; (iii) election to treat a partnership as a 'Canadian partnership' under s. 102 is a status rule, not elective, and hinges on partner residence; (iv) for hybrid mismatch arrangements, ITA ss. 12(5)-(6) and 18.6 apply automatically (no opt-out election); entities that are transparent in Canada but opaque abroad (e.g., a U.S.-checked-as-corporation LP) may elect foreign filing positions and disclose mismatches on Schedule 18.6; (v) under the QST regime, the operator of a partnership may elect to have the partnership registered as a person for QST, and partnerships with exempt supplies may make partial-ITC elections under the ar.A.Q.S.T. rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added tax: federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST, 5% federal component) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST, 9.975%, calculated on the GST-inclusive price); also subject to the Canadian 3% Digital Services Tax (DST) for large online-advertising platforms and the Quebec-specific rules for digital services and advertising (place of supply in Schedule IX, ETA; A.R.Q.S.T. equivalent).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the annual small-supplier exemption under ETA s. 148 (and corresponding A.R.Q.S.T. provision) for worldwide gross taxable supplies; for non-resident suppliers of digital services (including programmatic ad-exchange/SSP services supplied to Canadian recipients), mandatory simplified GST/HST registration is triggered once taxable supplies to Canadian recipients exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter (ETA s. 242.1); no registration threshold for a Quebec-resident LP that makes supplies in Canada in the course of a commercial activity once it exceeds CAD 30,000; the QST threshold mirrors the GST threshold at CAD 30,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or a mandatory continuous-control e-invoicing regime. GST/HST registrants must issue invoices containing prescribed particulars (serial number, date, seller BN, buyer name, description, tax amounts) under ETA s. 221(1) and Quebec A.R.Q.S.T.; electronic invoicing is permitted. Mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST returns applies to registrants with annual taxable revenue above CAD 1.5 million; Revenu Québec likewise mandates electronic filing for QST for large businesses. Canada is progressively adopting the Pan-Canadian e-invoice standard (PEPPOL-compliant UBL) on a voluntary B2B basis, and federal procurement e-invoicing is expected for B2G; until further notice, no fiscal-clearance API or pre-clearance stamping is mandatory for an AdTech platform in Quebec.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 of the Excise Tax Act, a supply of a service (including programmatic ad-exchange facilitation, SSP platform services, DSP connectivity, and data-driven advertising services) to a non-resident person is zero-rated unless the supply is in respect of real property situated in Canada, goods situated in Canada, or a service performed at a time when the recipient is present in Canada; additional exclusions apply for fitness entries, conventions, and certain cross-border support services. For the rendered supply to qualify: (i) the recipient must be a non-resident with no Canadian-administered stable base (place-of-supply rules in Sch. IX point to the recipient's permanent establishment), (ii) the contract and commercial invoice must identify the foreign counterparty and state the zero-rated treatment, and (iii) the same service supplied to a Canadian advertiser, Canadian publisher, or Canadian DSP/SSP is taxable at the 14.975% combined Quebec rate. QST export zero-rating mirrors the GST/HST rules under the A.R.Q.S.T.; the LP must keep evidence that the recipient is non-resident and, for services delivered digitally to a foreign establishment, maintain platform logs showing the foreign IP/user location and payment routing from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA G13/B13A Export Declaration (required only where tangible goods are bundled with the platform service; services-only exports require no customs export declaration)
GST/HST zero-rated commercial invoice showing the LP's BN/RT account, 'zero-rated export supply — Sch. VI Pt. V s. 7', the non-resident recipient, and the foreign currency consideration
Signed AdTech service agreement / insertion and campaign logs evidencing the foreign publisher-DSP/SSP counterparty and offshore delivery (serving logs, IP addresses, geo-tags)
Bill of Lading / airway waybill (goods bundled scenario only) replaced, for services, by platform export records and delivery confirmation from the ad-exchange server
Inward remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103, ACH export settlement confirmations, or the foreign bank credit advice (the Canadian functional equivalent of an inward remittance certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess zero-rated supplies within the normal 4-year reassessment period, extended to 10 years where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established, and may recover net tax, ITCs, interest, and penalty. Penalties: ETA s. 280(1) failure-to-file penalty of 5% plus 1% per month (max 12 months); s. 285(1) 50% gross-negligence penalty on any net tax understated; false statements or omissions attract s. 285(1) penalties up to 50% of the tax sought; knowing participation in a fraudulent export-zero-rating scheme is criminal tax evasion under ETA s. 327 (fines up to CAD 250,000 and imprisonment up to 12 months on summary conviction — the possible sentence for indictable is up to CAD 100,000 fine and 2 years? Let me use: 'substantial fines and imprisonment'), and Quebec's Tax Administration Act (C-26) authorizes similar QST penalties and criminal referrals by Revenu Québec. Export documentation must be retained for six years (and available within 60 days on demand); failure to produce contemporaneous documentation to CRA/Revenu Québec results in taxable treatment at 14.975%, interest, clawback of input tax credits, and denial of refunds. Although Canada imposes no statutory FX-conversion deadline, the 180-day inward-repatriation benchmark is enforced as a documentary and audit-risk indicator for zero-rating substantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), Ottawa — central bank responsible for monetary policy, legal tender issuance, Payments Canada oversight, and, as of November 2024, registration of Payment Service Providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA). Complementary regulators: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential supervision of Schedule I chartered banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CTF and cross-border EFT reporting; Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF), Quebec, for derivatives, trade repositories, and securities registration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The CAD is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts; Canada has no exchange controls since the repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1951. Inbound subscription capital, AdTech export service fees, operating liquidity, and profit distributions may move freely without central-bank approval, FX licences, or repatriation ceilings. Remittance hurdles are solely fiscal: (i) Part I tax on each non-resident partner's share of Canadian-source business income of the CA_LP; (ii) Part XIII withholding at 25% statutory (treaty-reducible) on management fees, guarantee fees, interest, or other Part XIII payments to non-resident partners; and (iii) possible CRA clearance-certificate obligations on disposition of a partnership interest. No CAD conversion ratio or profit-repatriation limit applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, no forced conversion, and no statutory timeline for repatriation of export or service proceeds. Cross-border receipts of the ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810 programmatic AdTech platform may be retained in USD, EUR, GBP, or any convertible currency worldwide, or settled into Quebec in CAD at the bank's commercial spot rate. The sole compliance obligation is transparency: every cross-border SWIFT EFT equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC via the bank's cross-border wire report; the CA_LP must maintain a complete settlement ledger to support EFT-report corrections or 'unusual transaction' inquiries.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility — ancillary liquidity rail only. Canada does not issue EU-style EMI licences. Cross-border PSPs (e.g., Wise Platform, Airwallex, Payoneer) must be registered with FINTRAC as Money Service Businesses and, from 2024-2025, as Payment Service Providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA). They may hold multi-currency balances, issue virtual IBANs, originate EFTs, and convert currencies, but are not chartered banks and cannot offer insured CAD deposits or Lynx RTGS settlement finality. Legal constraints: (i) client funds must be segregated in trust accounts at a Canadian bank; (ii) the PSP cannot lend or invest the float; (iii) virtual IBANs are valid only inside the PSP's own network and do not map to a Payments Canada transit/routing number. Recommended treasury architecture: use a PSP for receiving small-value non-resident DSP/SSP payouts and pre-funding, but execute all final settlement, escrow, and FX hedging through National Bank of Canada or RBC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted under FINTRAC's identity-verification framework. If the General Partner is a Canadian-registered corporation, the LP account may be opened via video conference supplemented by notarized copies of the partnership agreement and RÉQ attestation. For an LP with non-resident partners, any U.S. person (FATCA nexus), or a first capital injection above CAD 250,000, the bank will mandate a video call plus either an in-person visit to a Montreal or Quebec City branch by an authorized signatory, or a Canadian notary attestation of identity for each beneficial owner. There is no statutory requirement for directors to appear physically in Canada provided the GP is Canadian-registered and no direct U.S. person holds an interest; however, escalation to in-person presence is practically certain where any beneficial owner is from a high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or offshore General Partner; banks require identification of the GP and every partner holding 25%+ of capital; an opaque GP domiciled in a tax haven is a hard blocker.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RÉQ/CPEQ registration certificate; executed limited partnership agreement; complete KYC of the GP (incorporation, directors, register of directors); signing-authority resolution; sworn beneficial-ownership table for every partner above 10%; if the GP is non-Canadian, include local-counsel legal opinion and passport/ID of the GP's director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: U.S. nexus: any U.S. person or U.S. entity in the ownership chain, or U.S.-sourced AdTech inventory raising FATCA/CFCA and U.S. trade-or-business exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: W-8BEN-E for every non-U.S. partner; W-9 for each U.S. person; FATCA classification letters; IRS Form 8832 or 1120-F evidence if a U.S. corporate partner exists; narrative memo concluding no U.S. permanent establishment; Canada-U.S. Treaty LOB analysis for the U.S. partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border AdTech settlement inflows from numerous DSP/SSP counterparties generating FINTRAC EFT reports and flagged 'unusual transaction' patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated counterparty due-diligence file for each SSP/DSP (corporate registration, licence, negative-media screening); platform flow diagram; sample settlement trail from exchange logs to bank statement; CA_LP written AML/KYC procedures; named compliance officer in Quebec/Ontario responsible for FINTRAC reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from a third-party funded wire where the subscribing partner's funds originate from a shareholder, founder, or affiliate rather than the partner's own account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital subscription agreement; six months of bank statements of the paying partner; declaration of ultimate source of wealth; notarized gift or loan agreement for any advanced funds; corporate authorization of the paying entity; OECD CRS self-certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to non-resident partners that appear as dividends, guarantees, or fees, triggering Part XIII withholding and anti-money-laundering explanation requests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed ledger classifying each payment (income allocation vs guaranteed payment vs interest); Part XIII withholding remittance receipts to CRA; NR4/T1042 filing copies; explanation of the non-resident partners' Part I instalment arrangement; LP settlement ledger with bank confirmations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident partner's own bank account. Use purpose codes in field 70 as follows: /PURP/EQUI/ for subscribed capital into the escrow account; /PURP/INTR/ for partner loans; /PURP/CTRI/ for treasury top-ups. The remittance must name the CA_LP exactly as registered with the RÉQ (in Quebec, a limited partnership is a société en commandite, abbreviated S.E.C.) and include the Québec enterprise number (NEQ). The receiving bank verifies: (i) remitter name matches the executed subscription schedule; (ii) a GP resolution authorizes account opening and receipt; (iii) amounts above CAD 100,000 settle through Lynx for same-day finality. Where the wire arrives in USD/EUR/GBP, execute a spot FX contract (T+2) with the same bank for CAD conversion, or retain the foreign currency in a dedicated USD/EUR operating account if future payout legs justify it. All inbound EFTs at or above CAD 10,000 are captured by FINTRAC cross-border wire reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Non-resident publisher/exchange payouts: use SWIFT MT103 with field 70 purpose codes /PURP/TRDP/ for trade payments and /PURP/SERV/ for service disbursements, referencing the underlying invoice number. For high-value or documentary-risk settlements, arrange an Irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit subject to UCP600 issued by the Quebec relationship bank and advised or confirmed at the beneficiary's bank, payable against presentation of the digital delivery certificate, IAB/GDPR-compliant settlement report, and commercial invoice; expect 100% cash collateral for an unrated LP. Domestic Canadian settlements: use Lynx (RTGS, irrevocable within seconds) for amounts exceeding CAD 100,000; use ACSS (ACH-equivalent, next-day finality) for amounts below CAD 100,000. For USD-denominated flows, prefer the same-bank U.S. clearing channel or U.S. correspondent to avoid double FX; conversion spreads are negotiable from approximately 20 pips at annual FX volumes above USD 5 million.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot (T+2) contracts — no regulatory constraint; standard treasury tool with any Schedule I bank; used for daily conversion of cross-border USD/EUR settlement proceeds.

Outright FX forwards (maturities up to 24 months) — documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex; qualify as a bona fide hedge for a non-financial end user; exempt from central clearing; reportable to an AMF-recognized trade repository (DTCC Data Repository) within two business days.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — permissible for hedging CAD receivables against non-convertible publisher settlement currencies such as INR, BRL, or NGN; documented under the ISDA 1998 FX and Currency Option Definitions; execute on a margined basis to avoid drawing down credit lines.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS/CCS) — permitted for multi-currency funding and asset-liability alignment; mandatory clearing is waived for non-financial counterparties when used strictly for a commercial hedge; reportable to the AMF trade repository within two business days.

Vanilla European FX options — permitted when purchased from a Schedule I bank under an ISDA Master Agreement; the CA_LP must not write or sell options, as option writing triggers dealer registration requirements under Quebec's Derivatives Act (RLRQ c I-14.01) and CIRO; purchased calls/puts qualify as hedging and impose no registration obligation on the buyer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual enterprise declaration (déclaration annuelle) for the Quebec limited partnership, updating registered particulars including general partner identification, partnership name, registered office, principal establishment, and any change in statutory information.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (RÉQ), Ministère de la Justice, Government of Quebec.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the anniversary date of the partnership's registration in the RÉQ. The deadline does not follow the calendar year; it rolls annually from the original registration date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Prescribed monetary penalties up to CAD 4,000 for late or deficient filing; continued non-compliance exposes the LP to a formal default notice and administrative cancellation of its registration in the RÉQ, resulting in loss of registry status and inability to invoke the Quebec legal publicity regime in business dealings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 partner allocation slips (federal partnership information filing).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end; for a calendar-year fiscal period, the return is due by May 31 of the following year, while T5013 slips must be provided to partners by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the T5013 return attracts a penalty of CAD 100 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; failure to provide or file T5013 slips attracts CAD 25 per slip per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500; egregious omissions or false statements may expose the partnership to higher penalties and criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Quebec limited partnerships are not subject to an automatic statutory audit threshold under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A mandatory independent audit arises only when: (i) the partnership is a reporting issuer or regulated securities entity under Quebec securities legislation; (ii) an applicable regulator such as the Autorité des marchés financiers imposes an audit condition; (iii) the partnership agreement or a lending/creditor covenant requires audited financial statements; or (iv) the corporate general partner is required to undergo an audit under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Quebec Business Corporations Act and does not obtain unanimous shareholder consent to dispense with an audit committee review.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements prepared for the limited partnership must follow Canadian GAAP as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook. Public accountable enterprises apply IFRS; private limited partnerships and their corporate general partners commonly apply Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) unless the partnership agreement, a regulator, or a creditor requires IFRS. Tax basis records should separately reconcile to CRA and Revenu Québec filing requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a Quebec limited partnership, the annual UBO-style confirmation is integrated into the RÉQ annual declaration and the general partner's internal register review. Partnership-interest transfers are recorded in the partnership's own register of partners; there is no public share-transfer registry as there is for a share-capital corporation. The general partner must verify any 25% or greater economic ownership interest annually, record transfers and admissions of new limited partners promptly in the minute book and partnership register, and file any required changes to general partner identity or principal establishment with the RÉQ within the statutory update window. The annual RÉQ declaration serves as the formal confirmation date for the continuing accuracy of the registered particulars.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (general and limited partners, capital contributions, and profit-sharing percentages)
Register of Directors (of the corporate general partner)
General Partner Minute Book (including limited partner resolutions, transfers, and annual consents)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200–USD 1,000 per annum for registered office or Quebec enterprise agent services, depending on Montreal versus regional provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if no statutory or contractual audit is triggered; USD 8,000–USD 20,000 for a certified financial statement audit of a comparably sized programmatic AdTech limited partnership when required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate rate + 11.5% Quebec corporate rate = 26.5% combined applicable to a corporate partner on its allocated LP income; the Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and pays no entity-level federal or Quebec income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A qualified Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) that is a partner may benefit from the federal small-business rate of 9% and the Quebec reduced rate of 3.2%, for a combined 12.2% on active business income within the business limit. No AdTech-specific tax holiday exists. Canadian-source exploitation of intellectual property may qualify for patent-box-style deductions and Quebec innovation incentive regimes where the IP development has genuine economic substance in Quebec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T5013 Partnership Information Return (including T5013 Summary and Supplementary Schedules) filed through CRA E-File approved software or CRA My Business Account; the LP itself files no T2 corporate return unless separately taxable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned with the partnership fiscal period; individual partners report their allocated income annually.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than five months after the end of the partnership fiscal period. For a calendar-year LP, the federal due date is June 5 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 Box 15 — Net income (loss) for income tax purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the partnership's net income or loss after all adjustments, including programmatic advertising revenue, ad exchange and SSP/DSP commissions, and deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner, Canadian-source income is reportable only to the extent attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment or Canadian-source property; a treaty-resident partner should attach a treaty position where no permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 Box 20 — Partner's allocation of income (loss)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report each partner's share determined under the limited partnership agreement in accordance with fair value and economic substance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners must receive the T5013 allocation and, if the income is derived from a Canadian business through a permanent establishment, file a Canadian Part I tax return; otherwise passive Canadian-source income is subject to Part XIII withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 Schedule 50 — Foreign source income and foreign tax credit allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dissect foreign-source income and foreign taxes paid on international ad auction, SSP/DSP clearing, or data-services revenue for allocation to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner generally cannot claim a Canadian foreign tax credit for foreign taxes; relief is obtained through the applicable double tax treaty in the partner's country of residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filed T5013 penalties: CA$100 per day per information return, up to CA$2,500 per partner. Gross negligence or wilful omission can trigger a separate penalty under ITA s.163(2) equal to 50% of the understated tax, plus criminal prosecution under ITA s.239.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec Relevé 15 (RL-15) — Relevé des revenus de société de personnes, filed through Revenu Québec's online business portal (Mon dossier d'entreprise / transmission électronique).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be issued to partners and transmitted to Revenu Québec no later than five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end, consistent with the federal T5013 deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: RL-15 Box A — Partnership income (loss) allocated to Quebec
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the partnership's net income or loss attributable to a Quebec enterprise, including programmatic ad exchange revenue sourced from Quebec advertisers or publishers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner with no permanent establishment in Quebec should not report Quebec business income; treaty relief must be disclosed and supported by residency documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: RL-15 Box B — Partner's share of Quebec-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the partner's allocable share of Quebec-source income or loss, used by the partner in their Quebec income tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident limited partner, the allocation is included in a Quebec return only if the partner carries on business through a Quebec permanent establishment or has Quebec-source property income; otherwise no Quebec return is due for that allocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late RL-15 filing: CA$10 per day per form, minimum CA$100 and maximum CA$2,500 per form, plus additional penalties for wilful non-filing under Revenu Québec enforcement; severe cases are subject to prosecution and personal director/general-partner liability.
